findings.title: Migration raises NoMethodError when `embed_category` site setting row is absent
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings are only persisted when changed from their default, so on the vast majority of installs there is no `embed_category` row (and even when there is, the join on category *name* may not match). `PG::Result#[]` returns nil for a missing row, so `[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`, aborting the migration and leaving the deployment half-migrated. The same problem exists on line 15 for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup. Both queries need nil guards.

findings.title: Migrated hosts keep their scheme/path, so embedding silently breaks after upgrade
findings.body: Existing values of the `embeddable_hosts` setting could contain entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old spec and docs explicitly supported this). The migration inserts those raw strings directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` callback that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored value with `URI(referer).host`, which never contains a scheme or path, so every migrated row with a scheme/path will stop matching and embedding will start returning `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for those sites. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme and path) before inserting.

findings.title: Unescaped string interpolation into INSERT statement
findings.body: The host value from the old site setting is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Any value containing a single quote (or stray whitespace/CR from splitting on "\n" only) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration; it is also an injection vector from stored data. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized insert, and strip each entry.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table and its data
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If this migration is ever re-run (or a table of that name already exists, e.g. created by a plugin or a partially applied deploy) all existing rows are silently destroyed. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

findings.title: Host comparison lowercases the column but not the incoming value
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased column against the raw value extracted from the referer. `URI#host` preserves the case the browser sent (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com`), so a referer with any uppercase characters will not match a stored host and the embed request will be rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The parameter must be downcased (`host.downcase`).

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called before validation runs. If `host` is nil — which happens whenever the admin endpoint is posted without a host value (`host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` can assign nil) — this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` and use the non-destructive `sub` (the destructive `sub!` also mutates the caller's string in place).

findings.title: Hosts with a port pass validation but can never match a referer
findings.body: The validation regex permits an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` port and the `before_validation` callback only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:3000` is stored as-is. However `record_for_host` matches against `URI(referer).host`, which never includes the port, so any host saved with a port will never be allowed and embedding from that origin always fails. Either strip the port on save or compare against host+port.

findings.title: Host format regex rejects valid hosts that previously worked
findings.body: `\.[a-z]{2,5}` restricts the TLD to 2–5 characters and requires at least one dot, so hosts such as `blog.technology`, `foo.website`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or an intranet hostname are rejected. The replaced `embeddable_hosts` site setting (a `host_list`) accepted these, so admins migrating from it cannot re-add such hosts through the new UI.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host (possibly pointing at different categories), which makes `record_for_host`'s `.first` result arbitrary and therefore the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. There is also no index on `host`, while `host_allowed?` runs on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?`, which cannot use a plain index. Consider a uniqueness validation plus a unique index on `lower(host)`.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id does not exist (stale admin tab, double-delete, guessed id). `host.destroy` on line 16 and `save_host(nil)` from `update` then raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 instead of a 404/error JSON. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response (or `find`, which raises RecordNotFound and is handled).

findings.title: Missing `embeddable_host` params cause a 500
findings.body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises `NoMethodError` if the `embeddable_host` key is absent from the request. The controller should require the parameter (e.g. `params.require(:embeddable_host)`) so a malformed request yields a 400 rather than an exception.

findings.title: `embed: :ids` without `include: true` does not side-load the host records
findings.body: The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not put an `embeddable_hosts` array in the JSON root. The client's `_hydrateEmbedded` resolves `*_ids` by looking up `root['embeddable_hosts']`; when that collection is missing, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for every id, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. `embed: :ids, include: true` (side-loading) is required.

findings.title: `embedding#update` is a no-op that reports success
findings.body: The `update` action persists nothing — it only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will report success without any change having been made. Either implement the update or remove the route, action and the unused client-side `saveChanges`.

findings.title: Plural embedded hydration crashes on null and silently produces undefined entries
findings.body: In the new `*_ids` branch, `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if the serialized value is `null` rather than an array, and `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` can never fall back to `[]` because `hydrated` is always an array — if the side-loaded collection is missing, the result is an array of `undefined` values while the original `*_ids` key is unconditionally deleted, so the data is lost rather than left intact. The singular branch correctly only deletes the key when a lookup succeeded; the plural branch should behave the same and guard against non-array values.

findings.title: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, so a type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_admin_model`) will never match an entry in `ADMIN_MODELS` and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use a global regex (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`).

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this makes the fabricators impossible to locate by filename and will confuse every future change to either model's fixtures.

findings.title: No tests for the new embeddable host CRUD endpoints
findings.body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. The new `create`, `update` and `destroy` actions control the embedding whitelist (a security boundary: which external sites may embed the forum) and contain non-trivial logic (category fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, nil-record handling, error rendering), none of which is exercised. The same applies to `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. At minimum add tests that a host can be created/updated/deleted, that validation errors are returned, and that a non-admin is refused.

findings.title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer looks at embeddable hosts at all. This example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic, so the name is misleading and the assertion no longer covers anything related to hosts. Rename or remove it.
